routes.description: Map of route path patterns to the route each one serves (matching rules in docs/ROUTING.md).

includes.description: Other YAML files whose routes join this project; entry urlcode.yaml only, with no nesting.

policies.description: Project-wide policy defaults that every route inherits and may override in its own policies.

profiles.description: Reusable named policy sets selectable with policies.profile. A name shadows a built-in profile of the same name.

throttle.description: This profile's throttle policy, applied like policies.throttle, or false to turn it off.

agents.description: This profile's agents policy, applied like policies.agents, or false to turn it off.

security.description: This profile's security policy, applied like policies.security, or false to turn it off.

compression.description: This profile's compression policy, applied like policies.compression, or false to turn it off.

cache.description: This profile's cache policy, applied like policies.cache, or false to turn it off.

extensions.description: This profile's extensions policy, applied like policies.extensions, or false to turn it off.

site.description: Site conventions. Each declared key generates one native route (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, favicon.ico, .well-known/security.txt, llms.txt, 404.html); a declared route at the same path wins. errors is the exception: it generates no route and selects the JSON error format for a path scope. Entry urlcode.yaml only.

robots.description: Generates /robots.txt (RFC 9309). List entries are bundled agent list names or paths starting with /.

disallow.description: Bundled agent list names to shut out entirely, or paths starting with / that every agent is asked not to fetch.

allow.description: Bundled agent list names or paths starting with /, emitted as Allow lines.

sitemap.description: Append a Sitemap line built from the public origin (--origin); omitted when no origin is known.

extra.description: Literal lines appended to robots.txt verbatim, such as comments or Crawl-delay.

exclude.description: Exact paths, or prefixes ending in /*, left out of the sitemap.

changefreq.description: changefreq value written on every sitemap URL.

priority.description: priority value written on every sitemap URL.

sitemap.description: Generates /sitemap.xml (sitemaps.org 0.9) from active literal GET routes serving HTML. Requires --origin.

contact.description: How to report a vulnerability: mailto:, tel: or https: URIs, one Contact line each.

expires.description: UTC timestamp after which the file is stale; it must be in the future when the project activates.

policy.description: https: links to your vulnerability disclosure policy.

acknowledgments.description: https: links to the page thanking security researchers.

preferredLanguages.description: Language tags for reports, emitted as one comma-separated Preferred-Languages line.

canonical.description: https: URLs where this security.txt is published.

encryption.description: https:, dns: or openpgp4fpr: URIs for the key researchers should encrypt reports with.

notFound.description: Project-relative .html file served with status 404 and text/html for a GET or HEAD that matches no route. Generated as a page route at /404.html, which is also the object name static hosting uses.

errors.description: Writes runtime-generated errors (404 for an unmatched path, 405, 413, 415, 422 and the rest) on these paths as the fixed JSON envelope instead of plain text. Generates no route. A route's own errors key wins; handler, policy and extension responses are never rewritten. Refused on static hosting.

format.description: The error representation for these paths; json is the only value, since text is already the default everywhere.

paths.description: Exact paths, or prefixes ending in /* that also cover the prefix itself (/api/* covers /api and everything under /api/). Matched against the decoded request path, whether or not a route matches it.

version.description: Version of this extension configuration contract; always "1".

config.description: The extension's own settings, validated against the configuration schema its registration declares (urlcode extensions --json).

extensions.description: Versioned logical extension configurations. Requires explicit external operator registrations pinned to the project revision; never loads project code.

shared.description: Reusable named request and response.headers blocks a route selects with use. Resolved at load time; the route hash, audit and routes output show the resolved route. Entry urlcode.yaml only. Response headers the runtime owns are refused.

request.description: Request body checks a route inherits when it names this block with use.

response.description: Response headers a route inherits when it names this block with use.

schemas.description: Named JSON Schema 2020-12 documents in the request body profile, each written inline or loaded from a project file with {file: <path>}. A route's request.body.<METHOD>.schema and an extension such as mcp (a tool's inputSchema or outputSchema) name one by its key instead of repeating it, so HTTP and MCP validate against the same document with the same diagnostics; the OpenAPI export emits each named schema once as a component. A schema carries only the shape of a JSON value: authorization, query/path parameter coercion, display metadata and stored defaults stay with the route, the parameters, the page and the store (docs/HTTP.md#named-schemas). Names are a letter then letters, digits or _ (Urlcode... is reserved). Entry urlcode.yaml only. Each schema is admitted against the same profile, limits and diagnostics as an inline body schema, and its content (and every schema file's sha256) is part of the project revision.

additionalProperties.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 document in the request body profile (see request.body.<METHOD>.schema), or {file: <path>}: a project-relative .json, .yaml or .yml file holding one. A file is read offline: its relative $refs to other project files are followed and bundled into /$defs (a whole file as <stem>, one of its /$defs entries as <stem>.<name>); a remote reference, a path that leaves the project, a symlink, a missing target and more than 256 KiB per file, 2 MiB or 64 files in all are refused before serving. An object whose only key is file is a file reference.

methods.description: HTTP methods this route answers; any other method gets 405 with Allow, and an explicit list replaces the GET/HEAD default.

enabled.description: Set false to switch the route off so it answers 404 without removing it.

sandbox.description: Run this route's function/middleware in the isolated QuickJS/WASM worker pool instead of the trusted, in-process default. false or absent (the default) means trusted, unsandboxed, direct host-process execution.

sandboxReason.description: Optional justification for this route's sandbox decision, whether sandbox is true or false: why it needs isolation, or why it is safe to trust. Never inferred or enforced; surfaced verbatim by explain/context/manifest.

stream.description: Send a trusted function route's Response body to the client as it is produced (chunked, bounded by the operator's stream limits) instead of reading it whole first. Needs function; refused with sandbox: true and on every target except the self-hosted runtime.

additionalProperties.description: Why this method is tested elsewhere.

coveredElsewhere.description: Audit-only waiver: methods of this route whose normal-response fixture is provided by other tests (for example stateful create/update/delete). Each method needs a non-empty reason and must be one of the route's methods. audit lists waived pairs with their reasons under waivedRouteMethods and honours a waiver only once the route is shown served: another of its methods covered normally, or, on a route behind a sign-in gate (auth: true), a passing fixture asserting the gate's anonymous 401. It never hides a function route that only serves errors. Project file only: there is no CLI flag.

errors.description: How this route's runtime-generated errors are written: the 405 for an undeclared method (Allow kept), 404 for a disabled route or missing asset, 410, 413, 415, 422 and gateway errors. Handler, policy and extension responses are never rewritten. Wins over site.errors.

format.description: text (the default) sends the plain-text line, byte for byte as without this key; json sends {"error":{"code":…,"message":…}} as application/json with a code from a closed set keyed by status. HEAD still has no body.

expires.description: Quoted UTC timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) after which the route answers 410 Gone.

description.description: Free-text note for authors and tooling; it does not change how the route answers.

parameters.description: Path, query and header inputs the route accepts, validated before the handler runs; a missing or invalid input answers 400.

name.description: Input name: the {placeholder} in the route path, the query key or the header name.

in.description: Where the input is read from: path, query or header.

required.description: Whether a request without this input is refused with 400; path inputs must be required.

schema.description: Type and constraints the input must satisfy, a documented subset of JSON Schema (docs/HTTP.md).

type.description: Value type the raw input is converted to; path inputs are strings and arrays are query-only.

enum.description: The only values the input may take.

default.description: Value used when a query or header input is absent; path inputs cannot have one.

minimum.description: Smallest number an integer or number input accepts.

maximum.description: Largest number an integer or number input accepts.

pattern.description: Regular expression a string input must match, from a bounded subset that also needs maxLength (docs/HTTP.md).

format.description: Named string format the input must match, with the same checks and length caps as a request body schema: uuid, date, time, date-time, email, uri, hostname, ipv4 or ipv6 (docs/HTTP.md). Each bounds its own length, so no maxLength is needed.

items.description: Element type of a query array input.

type.description: Scalar type each repeated query value is converted to.

maxItems.description: Most repeated values a query array input accepts.

redirect.description: HTTP redirect. The route path may end in /** to redirect a whole subtree (literal prefix, one terminal **, no path placeholders, no conditional); no other wildcard is accepted.

url.description: Destination URL: a literal http(s) URL or a same-site path starting with /, where {name} placeholders are filled from declared path inputs and a subtree redirect can append the matched remainder (docs/yaml/redirects.md).

query.description: Which request values are copied into the destination query string; nothing is forwarded unless listed here.

pass.description: Incoming query keys copied to the destination unchanged; false or omitted forwards none.

map.description: Destination query keys, each filled from a declared path, query or header input.

from.description: Where the declared input comes from: path, query or header.

name.description: Name of the declared input whose validated value fills this destination key.

function.description: Run a JavaScript module for this route, as a project-relative .mjs/.js path or an object naming source, export and args (docs/yaml/functions.md).

source.description: Project-relative path of the .mjs or .js module to run.

export.description: Named export to call; the default export when omitted.

args.description: Named values passed to the function as context.args: literals, declared inputs or route bindings; omitted binds every declared path input.

from.description: Where the declared input comes from: path, query or header.

name.description: Name of the declared input whose validated value becomes this argument.

env.description: Alias of a binding in this route's env whose value becomes this argument.

secret.description: Alias of a binding in this route's secrets whose value becomes this argument.

env.description: Non-secret values the route's function and middleware read as context.env, each a literal or a granted process environment variable.

value.description: Literal value, never overridden by the host environment and needing no grant.

env.description: Process environment variable to read, which an operator policy must grant to this route.

default.description: Value used when the variable is ungranted or unset, so the route still activates without an operator grant.

secrets.description: Secret values the route's function, middleware, proxy and signals can use, each resolved from a name an operator policy grants to this route.

secret.description: External secret name the operator grants to this route; the value never appears in YAML.

page.description: Serve one project file as the response, with ETag, conditional and range support.

file.description: Project-relative path of the file to serve.

contentType.description: Media type sent instead of the one detected from the file extension.

cacheControl.description: Cache-Control header for the file; no-cache when omitted.

download.description: Serve one project file as an attachment the browser saves rather than displays.

file.description: Project-relative path of the file to serve.

contentType.description: Media type sent instead of the one detected from the file extension.

cacheControl.description: Cache-Control header for the file; no-cache when omitted.

filename.description: File name offered in Content-Disposition; the source file's basename when omitted.

static.description: Serve a project directory. The route path must end in a terminal /* (for example /assets/*); a static route without it is rejected.

directory.description: Project-relative directory whose files are served under the route prefix.

contentType.description: Media type sent for every file in the directory instead of the one detected from each extension.

cacheControl.description: Cache-Control header for every file in the directory; no-cache when omitted.

index.description: HTML file served for a request ending in /; without it such requests get 404.

request.description: Request body checks run before the handler; declaring it replaces the request block of a shared block named by use.

response.description: Literal response headers added to every answer; declaring it replaces the response block of a shared block named by use.

respond.description: Answer directly with a fixed status and an optional text or JSON body, with no code or file.

status.description: HTTP status of the declared response; 200 when omitted.

text.description: Plain-text response body; cannot be combined with json.

json.description: Any JSON value sent as the response body; cannot be combined with text.

middleware.description: Modules that run in order before the handler and in reverse after it, each able to answer early or change the response (docs/MIDDLEWARE.md).

source.description: Project-relative path of the .mjs or .js middleware module.

export.description: Named export to call; the default export when omitted.

policies.description: This route's policy layer, merged over the project policies; false on a key turns that policy off here.

match.description: Exact conditions every request must meet for this route to answer; a mismatch answers 404 (docs/CONDITIONS.md).

conditional.description: Several redirect or respond answers at one path, chosen by disjoint request conditions (docs/CONDITIONS.md).

cases.description: The alternatives, each a match plus one redirect or respond; their conditions must not overlap.

fallback.description: Answer when no case matches; 404 when omitted.

proxy.description: Forward the request to one granted HTTPS upstream and return its answer (docs/EGRESS.md).

signals.description: Webhooks told, best effort and after the response, that this route answered (docs/EGRESS.md).

extension.description: Name of a declared extension that handles every request to this route, typically a prefix such as /auth/*.

auth.description: Short form for a route protected by the declared extension that provides the request principal (the one whose urlcode.json declares providesPrincipal, whatever its name): true, or an object that expands to policies.extensions.<provider> with the same keys minus required; required: false emits no policy. Core owns only this mapping; the object's other keys belong to that extension, whose policy schema validates them (reported at this route's auth key). Refused when no declared extension, or more than one, provides a principal (name it with policies.extensions.<name>), or alongside policies.extensions.<provider>.

cache.description: Short form for policies.cache: the same object, expanded to policies.cache before anything else reads the project. Refused alongside policies.cache; use one form.

use.description: Name of a top-level shared block whose request and response.headers this route inherits. A key the route declares itself replaces the shared block as a whole; there is no deep merge.

routeAuth.description: The principal provider's route requirement, plus required. Only required is defined here: the other keys are that extension's own policy vocabulary, validated by its policySchema (urlcode extensions --json) at validate time and at startup.

required.description: Set false to document that the route is deliberately public; no auth requirement is emitted.

policyThrottle.description: Per-client request budget expressed like the IETF RateLimit-Policy field: quota requests per window seconds. quota and window are required once project and route layers are merged.

quota.description: Requests a partition may make per window before it is refused.

window.description: Length of the sliding counting window, in seconds.

partition.description: What gets its own counter: each client address, the whole route, or each client on each route (docs/policies/throttle.md).

status.description: Status answered, with Retry-After, to a request over budget.

mode.description: enforce refuses requests over budget; report only logs them so a quota can be tuned first.

maxKeys.description: Most counters kept in memory; the least recently used is evicted and starts fresh.

policyAgents.description: User-Agent policy. Named lists ship with the runtime; project-relative .json files in the same schema supply your own.

deny.description: Bundled list names or project-relative .json lists whose User-Agents are refused (docs/policies/agents.md).

allow.description: Bundled list names or project-relative .json lists whose User-Agents always pass, even when a deny rule matches.

denyPatterns.description: Case-insensitive patterns, from a bounded regex subset, whose matching User-Agents are refused.

allowPatterns.description: Case-insensitive patterns, from a bounded regex subset, whose matching User-Agents always pass.

denyEmpty.description: Deny requests that send no User-Agent

status.description: Status answered to a denied request.

mode.description: enforce refuses matching requests; report only logs them so a list can be tried first.

policySecurity.description: Response security headers. Profiles follow the OWASP Secure Headers Project; set overrides or adds individual headers; unset removes one from the profile.

headers.description: Which header profile to add: oshp, oshp-no-csp (the same without Content-Security-Policy) or off (docs/policies/security.md).

set.description: Headers added or overwritten verbatim on every response, taking precedence over the profile.

unset.description: Header names the selected profile would add that this route or project leaves out.

policyCompression.description: Content-coding negotiation per RFC 9110. Assets are precompressed at snapshot time; other bodies compress on the request path.

encodings.description: Content codings offered, in preference order when the client weights them equally.

minBytes.description: Bodies smaller than this many bytes are sent uncompressed.

types.description: Media types eligible for compression, with type/* wildcards; a documented default list of text and structured-data types when omitted.

level.description: One compression effort setting mapped onto each codec's own scale (docs/policies/compression.md).

allowWithSecrets.description: Compress even on routes with secrets or responses that set cookies, where BREACH-style leaks are possible.

policyCache.description: Named HTTP caching strategy per RFC 9111/5861/8246/9213; explicit fields override what the strategy implies. strategy is required once project and route layers are merged.

strategy.description: Named caching pattern that decides the Cache-Control output and whether the origin memory cache is used (docs/policies/cache.md).

maxAge.description: Seconds the response stays fresh (max-age), overriding what the strategy implies.

staleWhileRevalidate.description: Seconds a stale response may still be served while it is refreshed (stale-while-revalidate).

staleIfError.description: Seconds a stale response may be served when the origin fails (stale-if-error); emitted as a header only.

cdnMaxAge.description: Seconds a CDN may keep the response, sent as CDN-Cache-Control.

originTtl.description: Seconds an origin memory cache may serve a stored response

vary.description: Request headers the response varies on, added to Vary and to the origin cache key.

statuses.description: Response statuses the origin memory cache may store.

maxBytes.description: Largest body the origin cache stores

maxEntries.description: Most responses the origin memory cache keeps for this configuration; the least recently used is evicted first.

force.description: Allow immutable on a path without a content hash

policies.description: Optional host-enforced behavior around routes. Every key is off unless declared. Route policies merge over project policies; false disables one.

profile.description: Built-in (hardened) or a name under top-level profiles

throttle.description: Per-client request budget, or false to turn it off at this layer.

agents.description: User-Agent allow and deny rules, or false to turn them off at this layer.

security.description: Response security header profile, or false to turn it off at this layer.

compression.description: Response compression negotiated from Accept-Encoding, or false to turn it off at this layer.

cache.description: HTTP caching strategy, or false to turn it off at this layer.

extensions.description: Route requirements for declared extensions, keyed by extension name and validated by each extension's policy schema, or false to drop them at this layer.

query.description: Query keys and the exact values they must have.

headers.description: Request headers and the exact values they must have; names compare case-insensitively.

cookies.description: Cookie names and the exact values they must have.

host.description: Host the operator-configured public origin must have; never read from the client Host header.

method.description: HTTP method the request must use.

redirect.description: Where this case or fallback redirects, with the same url, status and query keys as a route redirect.

url.description: Destination URL: a literal http(s) URL or a same-site path starting with /, where {name} placeholders are filled from declared path inputs.

query.description: Which request values are copied into the destination query string; nothing is forwarded unless listed here.

pass.description: Incoming query keys copied to the destination unchanged; false or omitted forwards none.

map.description: Destination query keys, each filled from a declared path, query or header input.

from.description: Where the declared input comes from: path, query or header.

name.description: Name of the declared input whose validated value fills this destination key.

respond.description: Answer directly with a fixed status and an optional text or JSON body.

status.description: HTTP status of the declared response; 200 when omitted.

text.description: Plain-text response body; cannot be combined with json.

json.description: Any JSON value sent as the response body; cannot be combined with text.

redirect.description: Where this case or fallback redirects, with the same url, status and query keys as a route redirect.

url.description: Destination URL: a literal http(s) URL or a same-site path starting with /, where {name} placeholders are filled from declared path inputs.

query.description: Which request values are copied into the destination query string; nothing is forwarded unless listed here.

pass.description: Incoming query keys copied to the destination unchanged; false or omitted forwards none.

map.description: Destination query keys, each filled from a declared path, query or header input.

from.description: Where the declared input comes from: path, query or header.

name.description: Name of the declared input whose validated value fills this destination key.

respond.description: Answer directly with a fixed status and an optional text or JSON body.

status.description: HTTP status of the declared response; 200 when omitted.

text.description: Plain-text response body; cannot be combined with json.

json.description: Any JSON value sent as the response body; cannot be combined with text.

match.description: Exact conditions that select this case.

url.description: HTTPS webhook URL that receives a JSON POST, allowed only when an operator policy grants its origin for signals.

headers.description: Headers added to the webhook POST, each a literal or a secret from this route's secrets.

secret.description: Alias of a binding in this route's secrets used as the complete header value.

url.description: Upstream HTTPS URL with a literal host, where {name} placeholders are filled from declared path inputs; its origin must be granted for proxy.

headers.description: Headers added to the upstream request, each a literal or a secret from this route's secrets.

secret.description: Alias of a binding in this route's secrets used as the complete header value.

query.description: Incoming query keys forwarded upstream; all others are dropped.

requestHeaders.description: Incoming request headers forwarded upstream; all others are dropped.

responseHeaders.description: Upstream response headers returned to the client; all others are dropped.

body.description: Request body checks, keyed by HTTP method: each key is one of the route's methods and holds that method's policy, so GET and POST on one path state their own rules. A method without an entry has no body policy (docs/HTTP.md).

GET.description: The body policy for GET requests; GET must be one of the route's methods. RFC 9110 gives a GET body no defined meaning, so only maxBytes is accepted; maxBytes: 0 refuses any body with 413.

HEAD.description: The body policy for HEAD requests; HEAD must be one of the route's methods. RFC 9110 gives a HEAD body no defined meaning, so only maxBytes is accepted; maxBytes: 0 refuses any body with 413.

POST.description: The body policy for POST requests; POST must be one of the route's methods.

PUT.description: The body policy for PUT requests; PUT must be one of the route's methods.

PATCH.description: The body policy for PATCH requests; PATCH must be one of the route's methods.

DELETE.description: The body policy for DELETE requests; DELETE must be one of the route's methods. RFC 9110 gives a DELETE body no defined meaning, so only maxBytes is accepted; maxBytes: 0 refuses any body with 413.

OPTIONS.description: The body policy for OPTIONS requests; OPTIONS must be one of the route's methods.

requestBody.description: One method's request body policy: size, media types, format and JSON schema (docs/HTTP.md).

required.description: Whether an empty body is refused with 400.

maxBytes.description: Largest body accepted, in bytes; a larger one answers 413.

contentTypes.description: Lowercase media types a nonempty body may declare; any other answers 415.

format.description: text checks the body is UTF-8; json also checks it parses as JSON; malformed input answers 400.

schema.description: The name of one of the project's named schemas (top-level schemas:), or a JSON Schema 2020-12 document in URLCode's bounded profile, compiled once at load and checked after parsing (requires format: json); a body that breaks it answers 422 (docs/HTTP.md). $schema may only name https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema. Supported keywords: $schema and $defs (root only), $comment, $ref (local #/$defs/<name> only; never remote or recursive), title, description, examples, deprecated, type (object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null, or a list such as [string, null]), enum and const (scalar values), allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, properties, patternProperties (needs propertyNames with maxLength of at most 128), additionalProperties, propertyNames, required, minProperties, maxProperties, items, prefixItems, minItems, maxItems (up to 10000), uniqueItems (needs maxItems of at most 64), minLength, maxLength (up to 1048576, the request body limit), pattern (needs maxLength of at most 128 on the same node), format (uuid, date, time, date-time, email, uri, hostname, ipv4 or ipv6; each bounds its own length, so no maxLength is needed), minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf. Anything else, including $id, $dynamicRef, if/then/else, unevaluatedProperties, default and format: idn-email, fails activation naming the keyword and its JSON pointer. At most 8 levels, 256 nodes (1024 expanded through $ref), 32 $ref uses, 32 $defs entries and 64 properties per object.

requestBodyBodyless.description: A GET, HEAD or DELETE body has no defined meaning (RFC 9110), so this entry may only bound it; maxBytes: 0 refuses any body with 413.

maxBytes.description: Largest body accepted, in bytes; a larger one answers 413.

headers.description: Literal response headers added to the route's answer; only Set-Cookie takes a list, and runtime-owned headers are refused (docs/HTTP.md).
